model_output.verdict: A healthcare COO whose resume connects multi-site growth with operational and financial results.
write_up: This is a strong COO resume! You show the scale of Lakeshore Dental Partners and the work behind its growth, from acquisitions to integration and clinician retention. A recruiter can see both the business you run and what changed while you ran it.

The hygienist turnover line is a great model: it names the change and the compensation and career-ladder work behind it. Your progression at Midwest Physician Alliance and the earlier surgery center turnaround reinforce the operating story.

Your resume isn't the weak link here. Let's bring the integration result higher within the Lakeshore role and, if you can, add the company-wide decisions behind the operating plan. The competitiveness of a COO search and a referral can still matter.

cards.line: - Reduced hygienist turnover from 34% to 19% over two years through a redesigned compensation plan and a clinical career ladder
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a recruiter the starting point, the change and the two levers you used.

cards.line: - Own the annual operating plan and the $410M P&L with the CFO
cards.cannot_tell: For a role above COO, a recruiter will also look for the company-wide priorities and decisions behind that plan. Add those if you can speak to them.
cards.example: Own the annual operating plan and the $410M P&L with the CFO, including [company-wide priorities] and [decisions made]
cards.question: Which company-wide priorities and decisions were yours through the operating plan?

cards.line: - Cut new-practice integration time from 7 months to 10 weeks by standardizing the 90-day integration playbook
cards.cannot_tell: Move this above the regional operating model line. It shows how you made integration faster while the practice count grew.

fit.why: Your headline and current role both name Chief Operating Officer, and your work covers multi-site operations, growth and the P&L.
fit.level: Executive, COO reporting to the CEO and presenting to the board
fit.note: Your experience points to healthcare services COO roles, particularly in multi-site organizations growing through acquisitions and openings. The board and advisory work adds another view of your leadership outside daily operations.
